reason_if_not: The category cannot be built as specified because the named source holds no reference. The file https://people.brunel.ac.uk/~mastjjb/jeb/orlib/files/flowshop2.txt (13,908 bytes, sha256 616fa752381d9f4757a07abe0662b699fa6b69fefd1b354724825525c2e73d7b) contains no upper or lower bound of any instance, and no reference answer. Its only mention of bounds is line 19: "You will find lower- and upper bounds for the problems at Taillard's WWW page too". So "the upper bound stated in the file" does not exist, and Environment.score / reference (R2, R7) and a threshold (R8) cannot be defined from the named addresses. Taillard's own page is not a named address, so I did not fetch it. I did not type bounds from memory or use a bound computed by the adapter as the reference: neither is an external, pinned reference. The task text is also wrong on a second point, which does not block: the file prints no processing times except those of ta001. It prints one time seed per instance and the generator of the paper, which defines the times exactly. The form itself (R1) is exact. Nothing was written into REPO and nothing was registered.

checks.result: The file has 120 seed entries, identical in its two lists (Pascal part and C table). No line states a bound, an optimum or a solution; every instance line carries exactly one number, its seed. My re-implementation of the 5-line generator (nothing from the file executed) reproduces both prints of ta001 in the file, and an independent second implementation gives the same times on all 90 used instances (all within 1..99). 10 time seeds are used by more than one instance.

checks.n: 257 random partial states, 5 instances in each of 9 groups
checks.result: PASS on the draft: candidates equal the slow default rows and totals equal partial_totals at every state; rows of placed jobs are zero; complete answers evaluate to the same makespan.

checks.n: 270 valid and 720 invalid answers over all 90 instances
checks.result: PASS for the makespan and the validity rule, through decode in the instance's own labels, against an evaluator sharing no code with the draft (other seed list, direct congruence, full table). The score formula could only be exercised with a stand-in value computed in checks.py (a one-machine lower bound, labelled as not a reference): it agrees to 1e-12 and invalid answers score 0. Without a reference, score raises. The fixed-sample random makespan matches an independent pure-integer re-implementation on ta001 and ta045.

NOT RUN: the named source publishes no reference answer and no reference value. Mechanics only, with a stand-in equal to the makespan of an arbitrary order: that order scores 1.0, with two jobs exchanged 0.0, with one job twice 0.0.

PASS: one layout, ('assign', ordered, capacity 1 per option, groups (soft, detail), 0 var_attr columns, 20 opt_attr columns, no relations, no domain, no start answer). Instances with 5 or 10 machines show zero columns after the real ones; that zero machines leave the makespan unchanged was confirmed on 200 made-up cases with the independent evaluator.
PASS: the same own-label answer under two relabellings gives the same totals and the same (stand-in) score; the exposed rows are permuted.

Training 16: 100x10 2, 100x5 3, 20x10 4, 20x20 2, 50x20 2, 50x5 3. Fresh 24: 100x20 7, 20x5 8, 50x10 9. Groups and instances are disjoint. Halves of the fresh side: {50x10: 9} and {100x20: 7, 20x5: 8}. Two training/fresh pairs share a time seed: (ta072, ta043) and (ta058, ta086).

checks.n: 6 made-up training problems and 4 made-up test problems per design
checks.result: PASS with designs 'a' and 'b' on random times 1..99 in the same layout (10 to 12 jobs, 5/10/20 machines): acquire stayed within 40 constructions per problem and built a capability; all 4 answers per design were well formed and their totals equal the independent evaluator. The test meter stopped the learner at 1.03 of its limit each time and it still answered. No score was computed and no benchmark instance reached the learner.

PASS: the problem object is byte-identical with and without reference values; the largest number anywhere in it is 100 (times 1..99, sizes up to 100), while any makespan bound is at least 1073; the time seed is not in it. No actual reference exists to scan for.

Even the ratio of a lower bound to the mean makespan of random orders is 0.66 to 0.87 on every instance (lowest group mean 0.681 for 20x20, highest 0.873 for 100x5). A random order would therefore score above 0.5 on the plain ratio against any upper bound, so the share-of-the-way scale is the one R2 requires. Standard error of the fixed-sample mean: 0.6 to 1.6 time units.

open_issues: BLOCKING: no reference at the named source. To build the category, the owner must name a source that states the bounds (the task's description of the file, times with an upper and a lower bound beside them, fits the instance files on Taillard's own page, not OR-Library's flowshop2.txt) or decide on another reference. I did not fetch any host that was not named.

The task text describes the file wrongly on two points: it holds no bounds, and it holds seeds plus a generator rather than processing times. The second is harmless: the times are defined exactly and the regeneration is verified against the matrix the file prints.

Shared data between groups: Taillard reused 10 time seeds across size classes; 14 pairs among the 90 used instances are in different groups. With the same number of jobs (ta014/ta022, ta043/ta053) the smaller instance is exactly the first machines of the larger; otherwise the same number stream is cut into rows of another length. With groups as size classes, split(env, 16, 24) puts (ta072, ta043) and (ta058, ta086) on opposite sides. Whoever builds this must decide whether to leave out one instance of each such pair or accept it and say so.

The expected makespan of a uniformly random order has no closed form. The draft defines the chance level as the mean over a fixed sample of 10,000 orders made by a specified integer hash (no library generator). This is an estimate, exact as a definition but not the expectation itself.
The threshold is not set in the draft: it can only be an operating point on the share scale and cannot be fixed without the reference.

The reference meant (Taillard's 1993 upper bounds) is a best known value of that time, not always optimal; scores are cut at 1 if it is beaten. This would have to be said in the module text and the anchor.

The draft exposes a detail group (sum of finishing times), following jobshop.py and the kernel's convention for a largest-term objective. Like there, it tells the learner what each candidate job's finishing times would be, which the published instance does not state.

The draft adapter lives in WORK only. To finish it: add the reference source to the manifest, read it in reference(), replace the source path by fetch.path('flowshop', ...), set threshold and anchor, add the REGISTRY entry, and rerun checks (b), (c) and (h) with the real reference.
Terms of use: neither the file nor the description page carries a licence text; I did not fetch OR-Library's general pages, which were not named.
answer_form: Draft (exact, checked): AssignProblem, ordered. Variable k is place k in the order, the option is the job, each job is taken once (capacity 1); machines keep their published order, jobs are relabelled. Groups: [0] makespan of the jobs placed so far (soft; for a complete answer it is the published objective); [1] sum of finishing times of the placed jobs on the real machines (detail). Exposed: opt_attr (J, 20), column m is the time of the job on machine m+1, with zero columns for absent machines.
instances_left_out: 30 instances, ta091 to ta120 (200x10, 200x20, 500x20), by the size rule n_vars*n_opts = jobs*jobs > 30,000, fixed before anything was scored.
reference: None available. The named file states no bound for any instance. The reference meant is Taillard's 1993 upper bound, a best known value and not always optimal.
score_scale: Not operative without a reference. The draft implements the share of the way from the mean makespan of a fixed sample of 10,000 random orders to the reference, cut to [0, 1], with 0 for an invalid answer. The plain ratio is ruled out because a random order would score above 0.5 on it.
threshold_and_anchor: Not set. It would be an operating point, not an external fact, and it cannot be fixed without the reference.
